key_insight: ROSE-HEA predicts high-entropy alloy strength more accurately with fewer training observations by selecting experiments based on possible outcomes and worst-case predictive risk.
engineering_relevance: More sample-efficient strength prediction could help engineers prioritize costly tensile tests when exploring alloy compositions and processing conditions.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from alloy composition and processing using complementary Gaussian process models.
Anticipate how candidate test outcomes would update predictions and support for each model.
Select candidates to reduce worst-case expected predictive risk across a reference design domain.
evidence_signal: In retrospective evaluation on 501 HEA records across 30 matched runs, ROSE-HEA achieved 152.84 MPa mean RMSE and 0.7443 mean R² with 125 observations, surpassing the strongest conventional regressor's mean predictive performance using 185 observations.
watch_item: Results are retrospective; prospective experimental validation is needed to establish performance on newly synthesized alloys.
paper_title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
